# Go Numbers

<!-- Generated by npm run docs; edit scripts/README.template.md. -->

**Numeric validation, explicit parsing, range handling, decimal rounding and approximate comparison for JavaScript.**

[![Source line coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](#development)
[![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-100%25-brightgreen.svg)](docs/API.md)

- **Version:** [{{VERSION}}](CHANGELOG.md)
- **Licence:** [{{LICENSE}}](LICENSE.md)

Validate numeric values without implicit coercion, parse application input, extract
numbers from text, or control ranges and rounding. Choose finite or safe-integer
parsing when malformed or non-finite values must be rejected.

No runtime dependencies. TypeScript declarations included.

**[View full API documentation](docs/API.md)**

## Installation

Using npm:

```sh
npm install go-numbers
```

Using Yarn:

```sh
yarn add go-numbers
```

Upgrading from 0.0.1? See the [migration guide](MIGRATION.md).

### Runtime support

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Environment | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| CommonJS | Node.js 8.0.0 or later (`node {{NODE_RANGE}}`). Root, individual-function and supported legacy imports are included. |
| ES modules | Node.js 12.17.0 or later; Node 13 requires 13.2.0 or later, with `--experimental-conditional-exports` on 13.2 through 13.6. Default and named imports share CommonJS identities. |
| Browser | Standalone UMD or a CommonJS-aware bundler, targeting BigInt syntax (ES2020 or later). Both standalone files and their example run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. See [Browser](#browser). |

The package has no Node-specific runtime imports and installs no global polyfills.
Contributor requirements are listed under [Development](#development).

## Usage

### ES modules

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import { isOdd, parseFinite, getFraction } from 'go-numbers';

isOdd(-3);                           // => true
parseFinite('1.25e2');                // => 125
parseFinite('125px', null);           // => null
getFraction(12.345);                 // => 0.345
```

Default root imports remain supported: `import Numbers from 'go-numbers'`.

### CommonJS

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const { isOdd, parseFinite, getFraction } = require('go-numbers');

isOdd(-3);                           // => true
parseFinite('1.25e2');                // => 125
parseFinite('125px', null);           // => null
getFraction(12.345);                 // => 0.345
```

### Function imports

Each function subpath provides default and named ES module exports. CommonJS
returns the function directly. All forms share the root function's identity.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
import isOdd from 'go-numbers/isOdd';
import { roundTo } from 'go-numbers/roundTo';

isOdd(-3);                           // => true
roundTo(1.375, 0.25);                // => 1.5
```

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
```javascript
const isOdd = require('go-numbers/isOdd');
const roundTo = require('go-numbers/roundTo');

isOdd(-3);                           // => true
roundTo(1.375, 0.25);                // => 1.5
```

Named function-subpath imports require TypeScript Node16, NodeNext or Bundler
resolution. With legacy Node resolution, use named root imports or default
subpath imports with the configured interop setting.

The legacy `go-numbers/src/<function>` and `.js` paths remain available.
`go-numbers/src/Numbers` returns the root API object. The old `src/parseInt` path
is a compatibility alias for `parse`; it does not truncate to an integer.
Use `extractNumber` for embedded-text extraction. Private helper paths are not public exports.
On Node 12.17+ the package `exports` map blocks unlisted subpaths. Node 8 predates
package `exports`, so physically shipped internal files can still be reached by path there;
those paths are unsupported and may change.

Root ESM imports eagerly evaluate their dependencies in Node. Use a function subpath
for minimal unbundled loading; see [imports and bundle size](docs/API.md#imports-and-bundle-size)
for the bundler checks and their limits.

### Browser

Load the browser bundle directly from jsDelivr, or save it to host on your own site. Neither option requires npm:

- [Minified bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-numbers.min.js)
- [Readable bundle](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-numbers.js)

To save a bundle locally, right-click its link and choose **Save link as…**. Opening a link normally displays the JavaScript file in your browser.

These links use version {{VERSION}} and stay on that version when newer releases are published. The example loads the bundle from jsDelivr; to host it yourself, replace the script URL with your saved file’s path, such as `./dist/go-numbers.min.js`.

The standalone UMD files `dist/go-numbers.js` (readable) and
`dist/go-numbers.min.js` (minified) expose `goNumbers`, or return the same API
through CommonJS and AMD loaders. Both include source maps and licence notices.
They require ES2020 syntax (including BigInt literals) and the standard built-ins used by the API; they do not
install polyfills.

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
<!-- browser-example -->

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/{{NAME}}@{{VERSION}}/dist/go-numbers.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const { roundTo } = goNumbers;
  const result = roundTo(1.375, 0.25);
  console.log(result); // => 1.5
</script>
```

The readable file can replace the minified filename without changing the API.
The release browser matrix runs both files and this example in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.

## Behaviour

### Choose a parser

<!-- prettier-ignore -->
| Need | API |
| --- | --- |
| Parse a finite application value | [`parseFinite`](docs/API.md#parsefinitevalue-defaultvalue) |
| Parse an integer quantity without truncation | [`parseSafeInteger`](docs/API.md#parsesafeintegervalue-defaultvalue) |
| Extract a number embedded in text | [`extractNumber`](docs/API.md#parsevalue-defaultvalue) |
| Accept the complete legacy numeric grammar | [`parseStrict`](docs/API.md#parsestrictvalue-defaultvalue) |

`parseStrict` accepts numeric special values and legacy object conversion.
`parseFinite` and `parseSafeInteger` reject unrelated objects without conversion hooks.
Whitespace is explicit: trim at the application boundary when permitted.

### Numeric boundaries

Predicates do not coerce unrelated values. Genuine `Number` boxes are accepted
except by primitive-only `isNaN`. Numeric checks are not TypeScript type guards.

Invalid bounds, precision or options are configuration errors; validation still
runs when a checked value would otherwise be rejected. Legacy parsers can invoke
`toString`; configuration accessors can also run and throw. See
[behaviour](docs/API.md#behaviour) for these contracts.

Rounding uses shortest decimal representations and returns binary numbers.
Neither parsing nor rounding recovers digits lost before the call, and neither
provides arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic. `isClose` is not transitive.

### Callbacks and application validation

Use a unary wrapper when an API’s second parameter is a fallback or precision:
`values.map(value => parseFinite(value, null))`. Passing `parseFinite` directly
would use the array index as its fallback. See the
[callback examples](docs/API.md#using-functions-as-callbacks) and
[quantity-field recipe](docs/API.md#validate-a-quantity-field).

## TypeScript

Consumer declarations support TypeScript 3.3 or later; the compatibility suite tests 3.3.4000 and the pinned contributor compiler. Node16/NodeNext resolution requires TypeScript 4.7 or later, and Bundler resolution requires 5.0 or later.

Declarations support CommonJS, NodeNext ESM and bundler resolution. Generic
fallbacks preserve their type. Safe parsers can fail even for numeric inputs,
so their return types include the fallback or `undefined`.

```typescript
import { parseFinite, parseSafeInteger } from 'go-numbers';

const distance: number | null = parseFinite('12.5', null);
const quantity: number | undefined = parseSafeInteger('24');
```

See [TypeScript](docs/API.md#typescript) for overloads, option types and
the distinction between numeric checks and type guards.

## Performance

Primitive numeric predicates avoid allocation; boxed and unsupported values can
take more work. Parsing scans input forward, while decimal rounding examines
the bounded shortest representation of a Number. Conversion hooks and option
accessors remain caller code.

See the [performance and safety notes](docs/API.md#performance-and-safety) for
algorithm limits. The source checkout also includes `docs/performance.md` for historical
measurements and benchmark methodology.

## Development

Maintainer verification requires Node.js 22.16.0 or newer for the pinned lint tools and coverage-threshold
flags. Python 3.9+ is required for the full numerical-oracle gate.

```sh
npm ci
npx playwright install chromium firefox webkit
npm run verify
npm run verify:all
```

The coverage badge reports executable source-line coverage. The verification gate
also requires 100% runtime branch and function coverage. The documentation badge
reports checked reference sections for all {{CALLABLE_COUNT}} callable exports and
{{CONSTANT_COUNT}} constants; it does not claim exhaustive behavioural testing.

`verify` checks lint, formatting, syntax and metadata, generated documentation and examples, runtime
coverage, declarations, installed-package and bundler consumers, numerical oracles
and curated mutations. `verify:all` also runs both standalone browser bundles and
the README example in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. CI is configured for
Node.js 22 and 24 on Linux and Windows; configuration alone is not a passing run.

Runtime entries and declarations remain authored. `build` generates a complete,
self-contained `package/` with export mappings, ESM function entries and Node 8 wrappers.
The development root is private. To try a local candidate:

```sh
npm run pack:package
npm install ./artifacts/go-numbers-{{VERSION}}.tgz
```

`prepack` and `prepublishOnly` reject packing or publishing the development root.
`verify` and `verify:all` build and pack one candidate and reuse its SHA-256-identified
tarball. Pass an existing candidate with `-- --tarball <path>`; a missing supplied
archive fails immediately. Set `NODE8_BIN` to Node 8.0.0, `NODE_ESM_BIN` to
Node 12.17.0, `NODE13_ESM_BIN` to Node 13.2.0 and
`NODE13_UNFLAGGED_ESM_BIN` to Node 13.7.0 for exact runtime checks. `test:types`
executes compiled default imports on Node 8.0.0 (CommonJS), Node 12.17.0 (ESM),
and the contributor runtime.

Edit `scripts/README.template.md` for the overview and `scripts/API.template.md`
for the reference and derived summary, then run `npm run docs`. The pinned
development tools are TypeScript {{TYPESCRIPT_VERSION}} and esbuild {{ESBUILD_VERSION}}.

See the [contributor guide](https://github.com/koyote130708/go-numbers/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the complete setup, validation and release workflow.
